But, they ended up sticking pretty well. I guess you don't want them to stick so well that a 3-year-old can't pull them off. In my video, I show how they stick to a piece of metal, and they also stuck to my fridge, and all other metallic surfaces.

Also, once I took all of the magnets out, it took a long time to cram them back in so that the box would re-close. Forget having a toddler do this on their own, but if you lose about four pieces, then you should be able to easily fit the remaining pieces. But, I'd recommend throwing the box away, and finding your own box.

They have the numbers 1-20, with the corresponding number of things on the piece. For example, piece number 17 has seventeen butterflies.

Pros:
+Really sticks to a fridge or other surface
+Has the numbers 1-20, with a corresponding illustration
+Teaches new words like clownfish, cardinal, construction worker, flamingo
+The pieces are good quality

Cons:
-The pictures with larger numbers have too many things that are too small for a young child to easily count
-In order for a toddler to clean these up, you'll need to find a replacement box
-The magnets aren't super strong

Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. I'm sure there are cooperative ways to play too if that's more up someone's alley, like it was for us when the kids were younger.

text_fidelity_a:
Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

I do think, if used as intended, it helps work their prancer grip muscles, which need to be built up in preparation for writing. Unfortunately, either the size of the letters are too small and/or the size of the magnetic balls are too big, because when you run the 'pen' over the letters, they don't pull up the balls in the way/order they should (some balls that I want to pull up later come up already, and some of the balls fall back down). Also because of how large the balls are, it is difficult to actually 'draw' something recognizable on the flip side.

I thought my kids (3 and 5) would love this product, and that it would help them identify and write letters. They do like to pull up the balls with the magnetic pull of the pen (science, so that's good), and push them back down with their fingers, but after two minutes they lose patience and are shaking the board. Be warned this is not the best tool for learning to write letters.. there are much better and more satisfying ways children can learn that skill.

TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese) This tank model is superlative with a lot of details to glue on. ( it has no unnecessary steps that one hates and all the details are easy to glue on and there is no awkward steps that will make one curse while doing it) It take more than the time you expected which for an experienced modeler that is a joy t o add one after another small piece to the model and make it looks very real. After it is done it looks like from a $40 dollar kit than a 16 doller kit.
I have always learned something from other people's comment about how a model is made. Here I am going to recommend using epoxy glue for small parts of plastic details. The epoxy glue gives you more time than CA glue for small detail pieces. And the epoxy glue also have thicker substance than CA glue for small pieces so it will stay in place when the small pieces are glued on. The epoxy glue also becomes thicker as time goes on so you can adjust your timing to chose the right time to glue the pieces on to the model. The smaller the pieces the faster you need to glue on the model and the larger piece you can wait until is becomes very thick before using it. Another trick about dealing with those shining drops left unintentionally on the models; I usually drop some power ( you can use fine grain white pepper dust) onto the drop of glue before it is dried. This will eliminate those ugly sheen of glue and later the glued dust can be painted as rust for weathering.
All in all this little model (about 6 inches long) is well worth your money. It looks far better than other 16 dollar model kits and i can guarantee it.
text_fidelity_b: TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese)

Learning Resources Single-Sided Geoboard 11 x 11 Pin This is a fun, quiet little toy that is great for church, road trips and any time you need to keep a 3-8 year-old quiet. We took this to a family baby blessing and had the cousins not squabbled over it, the board would have kept my son very quiet! (And I mean things quickly deteriorated into a 5-cousin brawl of boys and girls ages 2-7 until the board was put away because everyone wanted it!)

Children LOOOOVE making rubber band designs and this 11x11 inch board allows for some cool ones. You can buy colored rubber bands on Amazon but I recommend grabbing a bag of neon bright bands for under five at an office supply store. The very few (like 12 total?) it came with were a rubber-eraser reddish-pink, dusty white and vintage spearmint green. They are fairly gross looking colors and except for the white, the rest reside permanently in the bottom of the rubber band bag.

When it arrived our board was yellow, which I liked MUCH better than the red shown but be aware you'll get a random color. The one we just ordered in October 2013 for a cousin christmas gift (since it was such a hit!) was also yellow. Every time my son pulls it out in church, children in the pews in front of us and behind us begin quietly peeking over his work to see what he's making with that contraption and everyone wants a turn! If you need a fun toy for kids of all ages that won't break the bank, doesn't require batteries or make any noise and builds brain cells while you play, this is it!

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab These days with many kids doing home schooling due to lockdowns, this would be a great home schoolilng science project or lesson.

The age recommendation is for children six and up, however since most of these experiments require the use of a pot of boiling water, I think the manufacturer should increase the age requirement. Parental supervision is of course a great idea. The booklet is easy to understand, however it might be more difficult for younger children to read and understand the instructions.

I only tried the first experiment in the kit and it worked as expected, and it was the easiest, fastest experiment to get results. The instructions were easy to follow. (I also lacked any distilled water which many of the experiment recipes call for). It was fun for me as an adult to try.

I am not sure if this is an option or not, but it would be nice if refills on the "magic water, colors, (maybe even some not available in this kit) and paper cones) were made available so kids (or adults) can continue to keep playing and making different crystals. (Alum powder and food coloring are both readily available at any grocer.)

The box is attractively marked and would make a great gift for any adult or child who likes science or educational toys. This kit is compatible with other chemistry sets available from the same company.

All in all, it's a fun, educational kit that anyone can enjoy. The only true down side is that it may try the patience of kids who like instant results. Some of these experiments take two or three days to have decent crystals develop. I liked the kit and found it fascinating. I can't wait to try the other experiments in the kit.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab

Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Pass the Stache Board Game The purpose of this game is pretty much to match "moustaches" with cards. Each player picks a "moustache" and holds it under their nose during the game. When a card is turned over that matches their chosen "moustache", they slam it down on the card, causing the attached suction cup to attach to that card.

It's a great memory game! If the player smashes the wrong card, they lose 2 of their winning cards. Each player has to remember which one(style and color) they have under their nose. It's also great for motor skills, since they have to aim for the card, possibly in a race against another person.

I was pleasantly surprised at how sturdy the "moustaches" actually are. (The handles remind me of a kitchen spoon/spatula handle.) The "moustaches" are larger than I expected and they're a sturdy rubber material. There are 6 different shapes/styles in 3 different colors(black, yellow, and brown).

I've had lots of fun playing this game with my newly 6 year old(delayed) and my 3 year old. My 19 month old has had fun, too, but he doesn't play by the rules. ;) This is a great game for some family fun. Laughs are pretty much guaranteed!
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday The car itself is pretty cool. I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...

Replogle Aragon 12" Desktop World Globe, Raised Relief, Up-to-Date Cartography, Made in USA (Blue Ocean) The review always asks: What did you use this product for?
Well, when we watch the network news at night, I never know, exactly, where the places are that are in the news.
When I'm introduced to a new person who has an accent I just can't place, and when I ask them where they're from and they answer with the the name of a country, that I'm not familiar with, let alone the continent it resides on, I feel like an ass.
And admit it, when you play Jeopardy (and 90% of the world plays Jeopardy) your palms start to sweat when the category is Capitals Of The World.
And you go into overdrive when the Final Answer is: What peninsula (peninsula?) is where the historic treaty of peace (what?) was signed in 2001 between the United States and the Republic of Whatever (OMG).
This replogle globe, which is Made in the United States, is not only beautiful but it holds lots of information. The Legend denotes swamps from canals and shipping routes. You just can't believe what you can "read" on a globe. If you want to know where they are and you are in this world, buy a globe. Buy this one.
Can you name at least three countries that survive Ukraine?
I rest my case.

Rockin' Rider Legacy Grow-with-Me Pony, Large Anyone who remembers the old TV series "The Lone Ranger" will recognize the title of this review. I give you my condolences because, like me, you are older than dirt.

My wife and I saw this Rockin' Rider Legacy Grow-with-Me Pony at our young nephew's second birthday party. It looked very sturdy, was colorful and well-built, and the children were lining up to give it a try. Since we had our granddaughter's second birthday coming up we decided to order one for her.

Safety is of course a big concern when buying something for any young child. However this particular rocking horse is well stabilized and provides extra protection as far as balance. Of course children can fall down at a moment's notice and for any number of reasons so it makes sense to always watch your child in whatever activity they're involved in.

Safer than the original rocking horse designs, painted with vivid colors, and having a very low center of gravity -- and thus superior balance and stability -- this Rockin' Rider keeps our granddaughter entertained daily, at least until she tires of it and moves on looking for other things to get into. Highly recommended as the safest rocking horse we've seen.

Deep Dilemmas - 'Would You Rather' Conversation Cards for Ridiculous Debates & Funny Interactions. 200 Original Ice Breaker Question Cards for Adults, Couples, & College Students - Ages 16+ I've picked up a bunch of these conversation starter games and some are better than others. I would say this one is right down the middle. It's a very straightforward concept - on each card is two choices and you're supposed to pick each one. The problem is that maybe half of them are real dilemmas, while the other half are no brainers. For instance - "would you rather live on a 50th floor penthouse with no elevator or have $2 million in dimes". These are the kinds of questions that might as well not be there because everyone just picks one of the answers and there's no discussion needed, which defeats the point of the game. In some ways I feel like they knew this going in - on the side of the box, it's actually printed that the playtime is up to 60 minutes - with 200 cards, that averages out to 3 cards per minute.

All in all, can't really recommend. You could probably spend an afternoon and come up with better ideas on your own.

Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

text_fidelity_a: LeapFrog Fridge Phonics Magnetic Letter Set, Pink I used LeapFrog Fridge Phonics when my children were little. Back then, it came with big chunky letters you'd press in to hear, "S says sss, S says sss. Every letter makes a sound. S says sss." (Or whatever letter you set in place). It also played the ABC song when you pressed the music note. We also had the Word Whammer that let you spell three letter words. The magnets were interchangeable and increased learning fun. Since then, I've always purchased LeapFrog products for the wee ones in the family. When I saw LeapFrog now had an adorable bus, I had to have it for my niece. It comes with the 26 letters of the alphabet and does everything the original LeapFrog did plus has some extra bonuses. Instead of just singing the ABC song, Leap sings two additional songs. He also uses the letters to create words and puts it in a sentence. (It's almost like having the Fridge Phonics and Word Whammer in one.) So not only is your child learning their alphabet, they are also learning how letter sounds work together to create words and complete sentences. The only downside of this darling phonics bus is the size of the letters. They used to be much larger.

Since this was a Christmas gift imagine the disappointment after within hours a couple of parts broke and I had to use packing tape to keep the box structure sturdy to hold the kit. The connectors for some of the circuits also don't stay snapped together very well, it is like some of them have a little bigger opening than others. I have heard such great reviews about these products and some of the labs are genuinely cool (like the fiber optic labs) but at this point I'm not sure what to do as it is probably only 50% usable of what I thought we were getting due to the build quality. Again great ideas and I'm sure others have had better luck than me and I understand that all products are not 100% perfect all of the time but this was a Christmas gift and I'm feeling a little bit like we wasted some money here on this one.
